header: Date: 2027-11-15 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 62 mins | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes | Labels: renewal, capacity, eu-region, security
summary: Call focused on Caldera Bank's upcoming renewal: discuss committed capacity increase, adding EU region for data residency, potential Dedicated pool vs Private pilot, SOC2/KMS needs, and concrete next steps (contract amendment draft, benchmarks, docs). Customer emphasized compliance and predictable latency for business hours in EU. Redwood AE + SE + CSM present; customer provided QPS/ramp targets and requested 48h perf run.
topics: Introductions; Current usage & pain points; EU region requirements and data residency; Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs; Latency/SLAs and cost; Security (SOC2, KMS, audit logs); Contract amendment details; Next steps and action owners
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna run 60 minutes ish, agenda up front. Uh quick intros?
[00:06] Liam O'Neil: Liam, head of platform at Caldera, thanks, I'll jump in on requirements.
[00:10] Sara Gomez: Sara, lead DevOps, I'm mostly here for the provisioning and network side.
[00:14] Marta Ruiz: Marta — security and compliance, I'll cover controls.
[00:18] Maya Patel: Great, Jonas and Hannah from Redwood, quick?
[00:21] Jonas Reed: Jonas, solutions engineering, I'll own perf/benchmarks.
[00:23] Hannah Kim: Hannah, CSM, I'll help with renewal ops and docs.
[00:28] Maya Patel: Cool, so to frame, this is renewal plus expansion — you mentioned wanting EU region and a bump in committed capacity. Can you walk through the current pain?
[00:37] Liam O'Neil: Yeah, so main thing is latency for European customers. Right now we route EU traffic to us-east and we see a, like, median p50 of 220ms and p95 in the 480-600ms window during peak. For regulatory reasons we also need data at rest in EU for some products, so residency matters.
[00:57] Sara Gomez: And we have some cold-start spikes when KV cache misses. It was worse during the marketing campaign last month, saw retries.
[01:05] Jonas Reed: Okay, that matches what we saw in the logs you shared. If we add eu-west dedicated shard we can drop median to ~90-120ms and p95 to under 250ms depending on model and sequence length. Those are estimates but we've seen similar customers hit those numbers with Dedicated.
[01:21] Liam O'Neil: So dedicated vs private — what's the tradeoff? Marta mentioned on-prem earlier.
[01:26] Marta Ruiz: Yes we have some customers needing EU-only storage and strict KMS control, possibly HSM.
[01:31] Jonas Reed: Right. Quick tradeoff: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in our managed infra, predictable throughput, and you can opt for EU-only tenancy. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you customer-managed control plane and full data plane isolation — better for HSM/KMS-in-your-VPC and air-gapped needs, but longer lead time and higher baseline ops.
[01:48] Maya Patel: Important to note cost and SLA differences too. Dedicated comes with SLA and simpler onboarding; Private is effectively an enterprise contract with deployment windows.
[01:58] Devon Park: For timeline, we need EU region live by mid-Jan for our payments product. Is that feasible?
[02:04] Hannah Kim: Mid-Jan is tight but doable if we start provisioning now and run a short pilot. The typical provisioning & validation for a dedicated EU shard is 4-6 weeks if nothing blocks. Private is more like 8-12 weeks.
[02:17] Liam O'Neil: Ok so Dedicated looks more reasonable for timing.
[02:19] Sara Gomez: Also curious about bursting — during Black Friday we have a 3x spike. Can Dedicated burst into other pools?
[02:26] Jonas Reed: Yes, we support burst policies: you can set baseline committed capacity and allow overflow into shared capacity or cross-region fallback. We can include a burst buffer in the amendment, rate-limited and with cost controls.
[02:36] Marta Ruiz: On security: we need SOC2 Type II evidence (latest), key management options (KMS or HSM), audit trails and retention for 7 years per our audit policy. Can Redwood provide those?
[02:45] Hannah Kim: Yes, we have SOC2 artifacts, and we support customer-managed KMS integrations and HSM options for Private. For Dedicated we offer KMS integration with customer key rotation and audit logs via Redwood Console. I'll attach the SOC2 pack and an architecture note after this meeting.
[02:58] Liam O'Neil: When you say audit logs via Console — can we export to our SIEM (Splunk)?
[03:02] Hannah Kim: Absolutely, we have log forwarding and S3/Cloud storage export options; many banks forward to Splunk or Graylog.
[03:08] Jonas Reed: Back to perf — can you share typical token lengths and model variants?
[03:12] Liam O'Neil: For the payments product, average sequence is short — ~70 tokens — but some reconciliation flows hit 400-600 tokens. We currently use open-llama-fin and an in-house reranker.
[03:23] Jonas Reed: Those long tails will affect memory/KV footprint. For 400-600 tokens we recommend higher memory instances and quantify for KV cache hit ratio. We'll put numbers in the benchmark run.
[03:34] Sara Gomez: Network — we need VPC peering and static egress IPs for our allow-lists.
[03:39] Jonas Reed: We support VPC peering and dedicated egress NATs; static IPs can be provisioned for dedicated clusters. We'll include the network matrix in the doc.
[03:47] Marta Ruiz: Any data residency certification for EU?
[03:49] Hannah Kim: We support region-specific data at rest. For Private we can guarantee full control; for Dedicated we can isolate to EU data stores and restrict cross-region replication by policy.
[03:58] Maya Patel: Ok let's talk numbers — you asked for a 20% committed top-up and add EU shard. What's the current commitment?
[04:04] Liam O'Neil: We're currently on a 1.2M token-equivalent monthly commit with ability to burst, but economics are rough because of the cross-region billing. We proposed 20% baseline top-up and reserved EU capacity equivalent to 30% of current peak.
[04:20] Maya Patel: Understood. We can draft an amendment that shows baseline increase and reserved EU pool. Pricing will vary a bit with the dedicated instance types; I'll include an illustrative TCO comparison (hosted vs dedicated vs private) in the amendment.
[04:32] Liam O'Neil: Would like to see a cost-per-token band and also a cap for burst spend so we don't get surprises.
[04:38] Hannah Kim: We can include a burst cap and alerting on spend. Redwood Console supports token-level cost-breakdown by route/model so you can set alerts.
[04:48] Devon Park: On acceptance criteria for the renewal — what metrics do we need to satisfy to sign?
[04:52] Maya Patel: Common ones: latency P95 under agreed threshold for EU traffic, no data residency violations, successful KMS integration (or HSM proof-of-concept), and a short smoke-test run with your test corpus.
[05:03] Liam O'Neil: We'll require p95 < 300ms for the payments flow and sustained throughput for peak of 1k QPS for 10 minutes.
[05:10] Jonas Reed: Okay we'll run a 48h throughput test to show sustained QPS and p95 numbers and share the telemetry. Expect KV hit ratio, cold-start distribution, and token-per-second metrics.
[05:23] Sara Gomez: Quick question — do you support per-route model pinning so we can route reconciliation to a larger-ram instance?
[05:28] Jonas Reed: Yep, model pinning and per-route instance sizing is supported; Redwood Optimize recommendations help choose quantization and instance size.
[05:36] Marta Ruiz: About encryption in transit: are mutual TLS and customer certs supported for inter-region comms?
[05:41] Jonas Reed: We support mTLS and client certs on Private, and for Dedicated we can enable mTLS for connections between your VPC and our endpoints.
[05:51] Maya Patel: Switching gears — procurement asks for a redlined amendment and legal terms for the EU residency. We'll need that by next Tuesday ideally.
[05:58] Liam O'Neil: Agreed, legal needs to review before the 30th.
[06:02] Hannah Kim: I'll coordinate with Legal and send the draft amendment and the SOC2 pack by Friday EOD.
[06:10] Jonas Reed: Technical note — during the perf run we'll test with your long-tail sequences and with a heavier context window; also we'll simulate the Black Friday burst pattern. Could you provide the exact test corpus and QPS shape?
[06:22] Liam O'Neil: Yes, I'll drop a link to the test set in the shared doc and include hourly QPS logs.
[06:26] Maya Patel: Great. Any objections or blockers from the customer's side?
[06:29] Marta Ruiz: Main blocker is KMS/HSM proof and long retention for audit logs. If we see the integration pattern and controls we're comfortable.
[06:36] Hannah Kim: We can arrange an architecture review with our security engineers and schedule an HSM POC if needed.
[06:42] Devon Park: What about rollback policies if the EU shard has issues?
[06:45] Jonas Reed: We support automated fallback routing to other clusters and model variant fallbacks. We can configure canary rollout, A/B traffic, and automatic failover to the global pool.
[06:54] Sara Gomez: Network egress charges — how are those handled in dedicated EU?
[06:58] Maya Patel: Egress billing depends on region; we'll include egress estimates in the amendment and you can choose whether Redwood covers inter-region egress for a term or pass-through.
[07:09] Liam O'Neil: Ok sounds good. Let's confirm the timeline: 1) docs & SOC2 by Friday 2) amendment draft by Tue 3) perf run week of Nov 22 4) decision/commit by first week of Dec?
[07:19] Maya Patel: That timeline seems tight but reasonable; we'll aim for it.
[07:23] Hannah Kim: I'll book the perf window with Jonas and loop in Security.
[07:28] Jonas Reed: One note on model variants — if you want lower cost on less sensitive flows you can use quantized variants in eu-west, we'll list recommendations.
[07:35] Liam O'Neil: Good. Also, who do we talk to if we need to escalate during the perf run?
[07:39] Maya Patel: You have my line and Jonas for SE escalation, plus priority support channel once the amendment is in place.
[07:46] Marta Ruiz: For audit logging retention, can you do 7 years?
[07:49] Hannah Kim: We typically keep 1-3 years by default, but enterprise add-on for longer retention is available; we'll include pricing options in the amendment.
[07:58] Devon Park: Ok that's helpful. Anything else?
[08:01] Maya Patel: Quick recap then next steps: I'll send amendment draft showing committed increase + eu-west shard + burst cap. Jonas will run 48h perf with your corpus. Hannah sends SOC2/KMS notes and legal docs. Liam will provide QPS curves and test data.
[08:16] Liam O'Neil: Sounds good, thanks all.
[08:18] Sara Gomez: Thanks.
[08:19] Maya Patel: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the perf window and the security review.
[08:24] [Meeting ends]
notes: Customer stressed p95 <300ms for payments, EU data residency primary driver, preferred Dedicated for timeline, Private if strict HSM requirement emerges. Agreed 48h perf run and contract amendment. Redwood to provide SOC2, KMS options, and billing scenarios.
references: SOC2 pack: will be attached by Hannah
